title: Load Balancers & Traffic Routing Algorithms
intro: Load balancers distribute incoming network traffic across a cluster of backend servers to ensure no single server becomes an overwhelmed bottleneck.
objectives: Differentiate Layer 4 (Transport/NLB) from Layer 7 (Application/ALB) load balancing.
Compare Round Robin, Weighted, Least Connections, and IP Hash algorithms.
Configure active health checks and seamless zero-downtime connection draining.
body:
### Layer 4 vs Layer 7 Load Balancing
- **Layer 4 (Transport Layer - TCP/UDP)**: Routes packets based purely on IP and port without decrypting or inspecting payload content. Achieves ultra-low microsecond latency and millions of packets per second (e.g. AWS NLB, IPVS).
- **Layer 7 (Application Layer - HTTP/HTTPS)**: Decrypts TLS and inspects HTTP headers, cookies, URL paths, and query parameters. Enables content-based routing, path-based dispatching (`/api/v1/orders` vs `/api/v1/auth`), and header-based rate limiting (e.g. Nginx, Envoy, AWS ALB).

### Common Routing Algorithms
1. **Round Robin**: Distributes requests sequentially across identical servers.
2. **Weighted Round Robin**: Allocates proportional request shares based on server CPU/RAM capacity weights.
3. **Least Connections**: Dispatches incoming requests to the server currently handling the fewest active connections. Optimal for long-lived WebSocket or database sessions.
4. **Consistent Hashing**: Routes requests using client IP or session ID tokens to maintain cache locality.
keyIdea: Use Layer 4 for lightning-fast raw packet forwarding at the edge; use Layer 7 for intelligent microservice routing, TLS termination, and auth offload.

concepts.title: Active vs Passive Health Checks
concepts.body: Active probes periodically query health endpoints (e.g. HTTP GET /healthz). Passive checks monitor live request status codes, ejecting nodes on consecutive 5xx errors.

concepts.title: Connection Draining (Deregistration Delay)
concepts.body: Allows in-flight requests to complete gracefully while stopping new traffic to terminating or redeploying instances.

examples: AWS ALB routing path-based requests to ECS container clusters.
Nginx reverse proxy load balancing upstream Node.js processes.

quiz.prompt: Which routing algorithm is most effective when request execution durations vary widely?
quiz.explanation: Least Connections prevents request accumulation on servers bogged down by long-running transactions.
